title: Impact of Nonnative Interactions on the Binding Kinetics of Intrinsically Disordered p53 with MDM2: Insights from All-Atom Simulation and Markov State Model Analysis.
authors: Xu, Qianjun; Yang, Maohua; Ji, Jie; Weng, Jingwei; Wang, Wenning; Xu, Xin
journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
one_liner_zh: 该文用全原子MD和马尔可夫状态模型研究p53无序TAD与MDM2的折叠-结合动力学，聚焦非天然相互作用对结合速率的影响，虽非典型TF-DNA体系，但蛋白-核酸互作建模方法可迁移至TF-DNA研究。
abstract: Intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) lack a well-defined tertiary structure but are essential players in various biological processes. Their ability to undergo a disorder-to-order transition upon binding to their partners, known as the folding-upon-binding process, is crucial for their function. One classical example is the intrinsically disordered transactivation domain (TAD) of the tumor suppressor protein p53, which quickly forms a structured alpha-helix after binding to its partner MDM2, with clinical significance for cancer treatment. However, the contribution of nonnative interactions between the IDP and its partner to the rapid binding kinetics, as well as their interplay with native interactions, is not well understood at the atomic level. Here, we used molecular dynamics simulation and Markov state model (MSM) analysis to study the folding-upon-binding mechanism between p53-TAD and MDM2. Our results suggest that the system progresses from the nascent encounter complex to the well-structured encounter complex and finally reaches the native complex, following an induced-fit mechanism. We found that nonnative hydrophobic and hydrogen bond interactions, combined with native interactions, effectively stabilize the nascent and well-structured encounter complexes. Among the nonnative interactions, Leu25(p53)-Leu54(MDM2) and Leu25(p53)-Phe55(MDM2) are particularly noteworthy, as their interaction strength is close to the optimum. Evidently, strengthening or weakening these interactions could both adversely affect the binding kinetics. Overall, our findings suggest that nonnative interactions are evolutionarily optimized to accelerate the binding kinetics of IDPs in conjunction with native interactions.
abstract_zh: 固有无序蛋白（IDPs）缺乏明确的三级结构，但在多种生物过程中扮演关键角色。它们在与伙伴结合时经历从无序到有序的转变，即“结合诱导折叠”过程，对其功能至关重要。一个经典例子是肿瘤抑制蛋白p53的固有无序反式激活域（TAD），在与伙伴MDM2结合后迅速形成结构化的α-螺旋，对癌症治疗具有临床意义。然而，IDP与其伙伴之间的非天然相互作用对快速结合动力学的贡献，以及它们与天然相互作用的协同作用，在原子水平上尚未被充分理解。在此，我们使用分子动力学模拟和马尔可夫状态模型（MSM）分析来研究p53-TAD与MDM2之间的结合诱导折叠机制。我们的结果表明，系统从初始遭遇复合物进展到结构良好的遭遇复合物，最终达到天然复合物，遵循诱导契合机制。我们发现，非天然疏水相互作用和氢键相互作用，与天然相互作用结合，有效稳定了初始和结构良好的遭遇复合物。在非天然相互作用中，Leu25(p53)-Leu54(MDM2)和Leu25(p53)-Phe55(MDM2)尤为显著，因为它们的相互作用强度接近最优值。显然，增强或减弱这些相互作用都可能对结合动力学产生不利影响。总体而言，我们的发现表明，非天然相互作用在进化上被优化，以与天然相互作用协同加速IDPs的结合动力学。
